newsitem.title: EGYPT: No discernible progress in Mideast - U.S. official.
newsitem.headline: No discernible progress in Mideast - U.S. official.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak held meetings on Tuesday in a bid to push the Middle East peace process forward before the start of a big conference, but a U.S. official said no concrete progress has been made so for.
Mubarak separately met Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher.
Christopher met Arafat last night at the Egyptian foreign ministry as the "troika" of European Union foreign ministers prepared for what could be a difficult meeting on Tuesday with the Israelis.

Commenting on the Christopher-Arafat meeting, U.S. State Departement spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters that there has been "no discernible progress," in a likely reference to the Hebron agreement.
None of the two leaders said they expected a last-minute breakthrough in talks between Israel and the Palestinians on Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
Egyptian officials said Arafat was due to leave Egypt later in the day. They did not say his destination.
They are all in Cairo for the third annual Middle East and North Africa economic conference, the third of its kind, which is due to open in Cairo on Tuesday.
The conferences were originally called to underpin peace by integrating Israel into the regional economy.
But the election of rightwing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in May has cast the conference adrift.
